posts.name: danmarshall14
posts.cooked:
Honestly, I have a gaming group that would really like this game.  I can see how the impromptu story telling genre doesn't appeal to everyone, but there is a large crowd out there that loves games on the more casual side.  Games where there are no points, stats, min-maxing, resource management, or moving pieces; where the entirety of the game stems from using your imagination and where "winning" or "losing" is completely overshadowed by having some laughs with your buddies.

Some of the most gut-busting moments with my gaming group have come from games like "Say Anything" or "Snake Oil" where you're making stuff up and not so much playing the game as you are playing the player by appealing to their interests and sense of humor.  I love those sorts of experiences, and while it's fun to sit down with a dense game of Arkham Horror or a strategic round of 7 Wonders, some nights we just want to sit around and use our wit to create dumb scenarios to laugh about.

Again, I get it; this style of game is not for everyone, and a lot of people likely look in on these games and think "What's the point?"  It's true that the experience definitely relies on to how close you are with your gaming group, what style of humor they have, their general creativity, and everyone's general mood, but I think that these sorts of games have a place at the table.  You certainly need to be willing to accept that there is no clear cut winner or loser, and even if there was, it doesn't matter at all.  What matters is getting some friends gathered around the couch, having some drinks, and laughing your asses off.

So, personally, I like the idea of an imagination-based story game with the Sentinels cherry on top.  That's exactly the sort of thing my gaming group would love to have on the shelf.

On another note, I'm extremely excited for the comic book!

The margins per comic book are incredibly low for the big companies.  Kickstarter comics tend to be in this price range, which is why they almost always incorporate a PDF version as an option.  (Although that is not always a good idea if you can get physical sales high enough to save costs)

That's just how margins work.  The initial cost to get to the printer is your big expense, once it is being printed each additional print in the run adds a nearly insignificant amount to the overall cost or the run.

Combining these two projects into one Kickstarter is probably knocking the price for each lower.

posts.name: Reckless

I worked at a small, greasy spoon coffee shop for about a year and a half.  Before it closed down I played a lot of Sentinels with my friends after hours.  The owner's sons, who were around five and eight, walked up to me one day and asked about the characters.  I told them as much as I could about the story and they were really intrigued.  I haven't kept in touch with them as much as I would like after the shop closed up and I got employed by my FLGS, but I imagine a game like Story War would be great for children.  I'll have to see if my 7 year-old nephew and my 5 year-old niece are interested in this game.

GSF's release was lackluster for me with all of the fiddling and typos, and Tactics is impressive but not my favorite.  BattleCon is awesome but came in an unwieldy, disorganized, and inefficient box for its expansion with Legacy.

Friends, have you actually PLAYED Pixel Lincoln?  You have to shuffle SECTIONS of a deck repeatedly and there are at least three different mechanics for conveying power up items in a sidescrolling Mario-esque world.  It's just my opinion...but if anyone thinks Sentinels Story War is the first instance of >G backing a subpar product, then I'd have to label you "uninformed".  Play Pixel Lincoln and get back to me.

The point is that I'm excited for the opportunity to show kids in my life something I love without expressing the difference between "put into play" and "played", or the differences between damage immunity, reduction, prevention, or redirection.  I'll wait and see what happens with this new Kickstarter, because Pixel Lincoln would've shaken me out of this company if I had a one-strike rule.

Fortunately the sprite art is great in Pixel Lincoln.  Unfortunately that doesn't make it A FUN GAME.

If you think I'm being somewhat off topic when talking about PL, I've at least played it.  I'll give Story Wars a try once before I start impotently shouting at the sky and claiming Greater Than Games have sold their souls to Mammon, the God of filthy lucre and terrible crowdfunded games.

My frustration has nothing to do with it being a bad/good game. It has everything to do with how SotM was handled, and how this is being handled. GtG made a decision about how they wanted to released the story and lore for these characters. Many of us look at all the pictures, flavor text, and come here every day because we love the lore and characters. Nothing wrong with this.

However, SotM does have a specific target audience, an audience that doesn't mesh with their other Multiverse products, and this is what is frustrating me. The choice not to give out the story outright, but to add in more hints in products that won't appeal to the SotM gamer. I have Tactics just for the added story elements that I didn't want to miss. It rarely gets played because of the groups I am in. Tactics isn't so bad becuase of the 5-year gap, but there is still a lot of info.

This trend seems to be going with Story War. I don't think It will get played a lot, since not everyone is a Sentinels fan, and I have better party games. Yet, if I want to know more of the story that has been hidden and secreted away, I have to buy a product I might never use. This is what is frustrating me.

WIth SotM, I have everything, not just because I want to support the company or being a completionist, but because I want to see the entire story that GtG wants to tell. In recent months, my resolve to do this have lessened drastically. Besides picking up Tactics, I then had to pick up the Video game to get a card, donate to a worthy cause to get another, and now pick up a new game I might never play.

I will admit that a lot of this is just me, and how I want everything, but the frustation is still there. GtG has chosen its style of storytelling, and how to distribute the story. For the first few years this worked fine, and everything was isolated to SotM the card game, but we still don't know the story, and we are needing more and more ways to get tidbits.

If you take a look at Tom's video, he doesn't say that it is a bad game. He says it is a story-telling game with its inherent strengths and weaknesses. However, he does say that there is no point in getting the game. You can have a better and more creative experience by giving everyone an index card and writing down whatever characters they want. There simply isn't enough in the box to warrant a purchase. 

That being said, you could play Sentinel Conflicts right now using the cards that you have (just get opaque sleeves). Even if you didn't want to mix the cards, you could just order some form the store and play now, instead of in June. The only thing you are missing is the art, and this is what frustrates me. I could get the experience of the game right now, but I would be missing the art. Essentially, that is all the game has for me: more art and story. Now, If I want to know that story, I have to buy more stuff that I don't need.

So, what does GtG do? They finally give us the story straight out, but couple it with the game. I actually love this dichotomoy. The KS has a product that finally, actually, tells the official story with a product that encourages you to do what you want. The book is $25, but you can save on shipping if you get both. Add on to this that there are no stretch goals for the books, and it feels like that GtG finally gives us what we want, in order to use it for something we might not. (I am not saying this is what is being done, but it is how it feels).

Now, if the book was being advertised as a way to learn some basic story for people new to the Multiverse and want to play Story War, I get that, I would still be upset, but I get it. However, there is nothing that indicates this is their approach. Which forces me to ask the question: who is this game for?

As I mentioned above, you have a lot easier time creating stories with the Story War base game, because most people know about those characters. If someone has no idea about the Multiverse characters, what exactly will they do? More importantly, will someone who has knowledge of the game want to play with them? I hope so, but I think it is a harder sell. It definitely feels like the game is being targeted to players of SotM, but therein lies the problem.

I hope the KS does well, and it looks like it will fund. However, the hardcore SotM fans (and GtG fans) are not entirely onboard. Both here and on BGG, the comments have been very negative. Nothing wrong with branching out and getting more people, but it shouldn't be at the cost of the current fans.

BattleCon is awesome but came in an unwieldy, disorganized, and inefficient box for its expansion with Legacy.

Reckless:

Friends, have you actually PLAYED Pixel Lincoln?  You have to shuffle SECTIONS of a deck repeatedly and there are at least three different mechanics for conveying power up items in a sidescrolling Mario-esque world.  It's just my opinion…but if anyone thinks Sentinels Story War is the first instance of >G backing a subpar product, then I'd have to label you "uninformed".  Play Pixel Lincoln and get back to me.

Yes, I HAVE played Pixel Lincoln. I own it, and the expansion. You have to shuffle sections of the deck once each, but that's exactly what you have to do for other games, like Pandemic. That seems like a pretty arbitrary complaint, and it definitely doesn't make the game bad. There are 3 different ways of using items. You can spend them for gold, or Equip them for their ability, which will do different things depending on the card. It's no different from Ascension or Thunderstone. You can also discard them for a suit ability, but this comes up so rarely it's basically an emergency thing.

Gameplay wise, it's a solid game. I was a bit disappointed by the lack of variety between the different items and enemies, but they fixed that with the expansion. It's not the BEST game, but I wouldn't call it sub-par.

See, when you say things like "if you don't think this is bad, then you are uninformed," you are saying that your opinion is the only right one, and that anyone who disagrees just doesn't KNOW, and that is a very elitist and condescending thing to say.
